meta.title: Nidra — Custom AI software for small businesses
meta.description: Systems built to fit your company, with no per-person licences. I automate the tasks eating your day, and what gets built is yours.

hero.title: The hours you lose every week
hero.lead: Typing the same data twice. Hunting for the file only one person can find. Closing the month by hand. I build the system that does all of it on its own, made to fit your company, with no per-person licences.

credibility.experienceDetail: Systems large companies use today, built and maintained by me.
credibility.ownershipDetail: No per-person licences, no lock-in, and no depending on me to keep using it.
credibility.locationDetail: Buenos Aires. I work remotely with companies across Argentina and Latin America.

pain.title: What you already pay for
pain.titleAccent: that never shows up on an invoice
pain.lead: You don't need an AI project to know something is costing you. These are the most common signs in a company under 50 people.

items.title: The same data, typed in twice
items.body: From email to spreadsheet, from spreadsheet to your system. Every hop is minutes, and an error that shows up at month end.

items.title: Licences built for a different company
items.body: Charged per person per month. Forty features shipped, six actually used. You pay the scale of a company ten times your size.

items.title: Everything goes through one person
items.body: The one who knows where things are and how they were done. When they take leave, the company slows down.

items.title: Month-end close is a race
items.body: Reconcile, review, correct. It ends late at night with the spreadsheet open, and something is always missing.

items.title: You hear «AI» all day
items.body: And nobody tells you what's useful to you, what it costs, or where to start without wasting money.

pain.cost: Repetitive admin work takes between 4 and 8 hours per week, per person. You already pay for that time in salaries.

services.title: Six services,
services.lead: Each one fixes something you can point at in your company. If what you need is not here, I say so.

process.title: Measure first,
process.lead: The order matters. Most projects fail because building starts before anyone knows what problem it solves.

steps.title: Assessment
steps.body: Two or three weeks looking at how your company works today, with real numbers. You leave with a list of what to fix first, and what to leave alone.

steps.title: Definition
steps.body: Before any building starts, I write down what will be done and how you will know it works. It is in writing and it is yours.

steps.title: Build
steps.body: You see something working every week, not a demo at the end. Every delivery checks itself before it reaches you.

steps.title: Production
steps.body: It ends up genuinely running, with alerts if something breaks and a manual of how it is built. All in your name.

investment.title: This isn't measured in price.
investment.titleAccent: It's measured in months to pay back.
investment.lead: Think of the task that eats the most time. Count the hours it takes each week and multiply by what that hour is worth in your company. That is the monthly saving.

items.title: Quoted by effort, not by your size
items.body: The price comes from the hours the work takes, estimated and written down before starting. It does not go up because your company bills more.

items.title: Only what you use gets built
items.body: No features that ship in the package and nobody opens. That is what brings the price down against a program bought off the shelf.

items.title: The system ends up in your name
items.body: No per-person licences and no lock-in. If tomorrow you want someone else to carry it on, they can: it is documented and in your hands.

items.title: It starts small and verifiable
items.body: The assessment is a short piece of work with its own result. You leave with the list of what is worth fixing and how long it would take.

investment.close: I don't publish prices because a number means nothing without your process in front of it. Tell me what you want to solve and I'll send the quote in writing. If it doesn't add up, I'll say so and we stop there.

technologies.note: I work on these platforms. I am not a commercial partner and I am not certified by them: they are the tools I build with.

founder.title: Nidra is new. The experience behind it is not.
founder.lead: I am Juan Mujica, a software engineer with {years} years of work behind me, now focused on making artificial intelligence genuinely useful inside a company. I work on my own: there is no team behind this, and no clients of my own to show yet. What you can verify is where I spent each of those years.

closing.title: How many hours a week go into something that could run on its own?
closing.lead: Tell me which task it is. In 30 minutes you'll know whether it can be fixed, what it would cost and how long it takes to pay for itself. If it isn't worth it, I'll say so.

meta.title: Privacy policy — Nidra
meta.description: What personal data I collect, why, how long I keep it and how to exercise your rights.

sections.title: What I collect
body: I collect only what you give in the contact form: name, email, company (optional), the service you're asking about and the text of your message.
This site uses no cookies and no persistent tracking identifiers. That's why you won't find a consent banner: there is nothing to consent to.
I measure visits in aggregate and anonymously, without personal data and without any ability to work out who you are or follow you across sites.

sections.title: What I use it for
body: Only to answer your enquiry. I don't use your data for advertising, I don't combine it with other sources, and I don't sell or hand it to third parties for commercial purposes.

sections.title: How long I keep it
body: The site stores no enquiries in any database. The message is delivered to my mailbox, and its retention is governed by my mail management, where it is kept for the duration of the commercial conversation and for at most two years.
If you ask me to delete it sooner, I do.

sections.title: Third-party services
body: I use a transactional email provider to deliver messages, which processes the message in order to get it to my mailbox.
If you book a meeting, scheduling happens on an external calendar platform. Any data you enter there is governed by that provider's privacy policy, not by this one.
Visit measurement is performed by Vercel Analytics, which collects aggregated, anonymous data with no cookies and no persistent identifiers.
If I add a conversational assistant in the future, I will update this policy before putting it into operation, stating what data it collects and why.

sections.title: Your rights
body: You can ask me for access to the data I hold about you, its correction or its deletion. Write to jmujica@nidra.cloud and I'll respond within the timeframes set by applicable law.
In Argentina, the supervisory authority for personal data is the Agencia de Acceso a la Información Pública.

meta.title: Terms of use — Nidra
meta.description: Terms of use for the Nidra website.

sections.title: Scope of this site
body: This site describes Nidra's services for information purposes. Its content is not a contractual offer or a quote: the scope, timeline and price of any work are agreed in writing case by case.

sections.title: Timelines and estimates
body: The timelines published in the services section are estimates based on work of comparable scope. A project's actual timeline depends on its scope, on the availability of information and on client dependencies, and is confirmed when the work is agreed.

sections.title: Third-party trademarks
body: The names of platforms, products and companies mentioned on this site belong to their respective owners and are used nominatively, solely to describe which technologies I work with or which systems I can integrate.
Their mention implies no commercial partnership, certification, sponsorship or endorsement of Nidra by those organisations.

sections.title: Ownership of content
body: The text and design of this site are the property of Nidra. You may quote them with attribution and a link to the source.

sections.title: Changes
